profiles.meeting_scenario: A design review at an asset-management firm's quantitative products group for a proposal to incorporate a homogeneously saturated stochastic asset-price model into the firm's equity scenario engine. The proposal compares the saturated model against the team's current standard diffusion model and a logistic variant, using Student's t-distributed shocks and historical evidence from DJIA and S&P 500 daily returns. The meeting agenda is to review whether the design is suitable for the next implementation stage, whether the benchmark evidence is adequate for internal approval, and what modifications are needed before the model is marked ready. The expected outcome is a decision on conditional approval for a near-term pilot and a short list of follow-up changes.

members.name: Elena Park
members.expertise: Stochastic modeling, market microstructure, and model validation for equity risk engines
members.background: Elena has a PhD in applied physics and spent eight years building quantitative models for derivatives desks before leading the firm's central research team.
members.private_state: She wants the design review to end with approval to move the model into the next governance gate without reopening the core research argument, and she is especially concerned that engineering requests do not force a redesign of the state-update logic.
hidden_assumptions: A 'pilot' means a research-only shadow deployment that runs alongside the existing overnight scenario engine and is not yet visible to portfolio managers.

The 'index benchmark' for this proposal is the close-to-close price-index series used in the academic comparison, specifically DJIA and S&P 500 daily returns as raw market observables rather than platform-normalized return feeds.
A 'daily run' means one end-of-day simulation cycle with the saturation state variables updated once per market close.

If the model is described as 'tail-consistent,' it means the raw simulated one-day returns naturally stay broadly within the empirically observed range of about -30% to +30% without artificial clipping or reporting adjustments.

members.name: David Moreno
members.expertise: Production analytics systems, risk workflow design, and internal product rollout for investment teams
members.background: David previously led market-risk infrastructure at a broker-dealer and now oversees the firm's scenario platform used by PMs, risk teams, and client solutions.
members.private_state: He wants anything approved here to fit the current platform with minimal bespoke infrastructure and to be usable quickly by investment teams, because his roadmap is already crowded with regulatory and client-facing deliverables.
hidden_assumptions: A 'pilot' means an internal beta exposed in the portfolio analytics interface for a limited set of PMs, even if governance language still calls it a pilot.

The 'index benchmark' means the firm's existing SPX and INDU validation series pulled from the platform data layer, which are calendar-aligned and use the standard return feed already consumed by risk reports.
A 'daily run' means the model can plug into the current one-day horizon Monte Carlo service that recalculates multiple times during the day while still labeling outputs as daily scenarios.

If the model is 'tail-consistent,' it means the reported scenario summaries fit existing governance templates and do not show implausible extremes after the platform's standard presentation and aggregation conventions are applied.

misalignment_points.surface_form: Both discuss getting the model 'ready for pilot' next month.
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: Elena means a shadow-mode research deployment that runs overnight beside the current engine for internal comparison only.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: David means a limited but user-visible beta in the portfolio analytics platform for selected portfolio managers.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: In business design reviews, 'pilot' is a routine bridge term that sounds sufficiently concrete, and both options are plausible next steps after approval, so neither participant feels a need to unpack the exposure level.

misalignment_points.topic: Which benchmark index series is being referenced
misalignment_points.surface_form: Both refer to validating against 'the S&P/Dow benchmark evidence' and 'the index series we already cited.'
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: Elena is thinking of the historical close-to-close DJIA and S&P 500 price-index returns used in the research note's comparison with the saturated model.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: David is thinking of the firm's platform benchmark feeds for SPX and INDU that are calendar-standardized and used in existing validation dashboards.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: The benchmark names sound identical at the meeting table, and both versions are legitimate institutional references to the same indices, so the distinction hides behind shared ticker-level language.

misalignment_points.topic: How the daily model will actually be run
misalignment_points.surface_form: Both agree the design should support the 'daily scenario run' and 'one-day horizon outputs.'
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: Elena assumes an overnight batch process where the coupled money-supply and price state variables are advanced once per day using end-of-day inputs.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: David assumes the model will be wired into the existing intraday Monte Carlo service, which recomputes one-day horizon scenarios several times during the trading day without a bespoke batch path.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: The team already has a one-day scenario service, so saying 'daily run' feels like obvious operational shorthand, even though the model's state-update cadence is materially different from the platform's normal execution pattern.

misalignment_points.surface_form: Both say the saturated model's tails are 'consistent with observed index returns' and therefore acceptable.
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: Elena means the raw simulated return distribution itself behaves realistically, staying within the empirically observed band of roughly -30% to +30% under Student's t shocks.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: David means the reported output will look acceptable in governance packs because the scenario summaries, charts, and percentile tables stay within customary presentation bounds after standard reporting treatment.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: Both are using the same approval language around realism and consistency, and design reviews often mix model behavior with reporting readiness, allowing a substantive standards gap to pass as normal alignment.
